question_or_proposition: Whether the Part I prohibition on discharge of oils, scum, grease, and other floating materials that would cause visible sheen, visible bottom or shoreline deposits, or damage to human, animal, plant, or aquatic life establishes prescribed monitoring or DMR-reportable parameters, or applies solely as a qualitative effluent limitation without associated monitoring requirements.
required_context: Part I section heading 'FLOATING SOLIDS OR VISIBLE FOAM' and its placement within Part I effluent limitations
Absence of a monitoring frequency or parameter table for this provision, contrasted with the WET testing table on the adjacent page
Footnote reference to Part II.B for best management practices and discharge restrictions
The general DMR reporting requirements in the immediately following subsection on the same page
notes: The nominated span is a qualitative, non-numeric prohibition without an explicit monitoring schedule in the visible structural context. Resolving whether it carries monitoring or reporting obligations versus functioning only as a qualitative limit affects limit applicability classification (Purpose A), whether monitoring was required (Purpose B), and how to treat missing or non-numeric evidence (Purpose C).
